entries.title: Nehemiah 3:1
segments: The sheep-gate; n the eastern part of the city near the temple, where sheep were sold for the sacrifices.  Compare

. 
 
In works of public reformation and such as are required for the protection and prosperity of the church, ministers of religion should take the lead, and set an example which may be safely and usefully followed.

entries.title: Nehemiah 3:5
segments:
Put not their necks; did not assist Nehemiah in the building of the wall. 
 
Men of rank often excuse themselves from the performance of those labors which the public good requires, and in which others are engaged; and thus neglect the talents with which they are intrusted, and set an example mischievous to all within their influence.

entries.title: Nehemiah 3:7
segments: The throne of the governor; the place where he administered justice.

entries.title: Nehemiah 3:8
segments: Persons of all trades and professions may assist in promoting the cause of God, and each should endeavor faithfully to perform that which belongs to him, and which his condition fits him to accomplish.

entries.title: Nehemiah 3:12
segments: When rulers and people of both sexes engage in works of beneficence, all doing what is appropriate to their condition, the work of the Lord will prosper and the highest good be effectually advance.

entries.title: Nehemiah 3:14
segments: The dung-gate; on the south-west side.

entries.title: Nehemiah 3:15
segments: The gate of the fountain; near the pool of Siloam, at the south-east part of the city.

entries.title: Nehemiah 3:26
segments: Ophel; an elevation with a tower, south of Moriah.

entries.title: Nehemiah 3:28
segments: Division of labor, and assigning to each one that which peculiarly belongs to him, and which he can most readily perform, prevents confusion, promotes dispatch, and tends to the most speedy and thorough accomplishment of every good work.

entries.title: Nehemiah 3:32
segments: The sheep-gate; the place where they began to build.  Thus they had surrounded the whole city.
